design.concept: A two-column desk for the team manager: on the left the queue of pending expenses (the primary work surface, always visible), on the right one expense read like a memo (who, decisive facts, description, history) with the decision block at the very end. Choosing a row in the queue loads the memo; the decision is a deliberate, single beat per outcome.
design.decisions: One view, no scene host: the queue must stay visible while the memo is read, so a side-by-side layout is the right tool. The queue uses the plain data table (internal mode, rows marked by index through `value`, `rowClick` selects) and a 'load more' button when the backend says there are more rows; no pager fields are shown. The right panel follows the readAndDecide template: identity line (collaborator name + status chip), decisive facts (date, category, large amount), narrative (description), quiet history (resubmission and previous rejection reason), then the decision block last, not sticky. Approve opens one native confirmation dialog restating collaborator, category and amount; reject expands an inline reason field (native details disclosure, so the page keeps no state) and its button stays disabled until the reason has text. While a command runs the block is locked with a live status; failures show in the block, above the buttons, with the reason kept. After a decision the block becomes a calm statement of the new status, and nothing auto-advances. Reject is secondary, never danger-styled. Search by collaborator/category and the period filter were left out because the shared exposes no state or request for filtering; the receipt viewer was left out because the expense contract carries no receipt field. Empty, loading and error states are designed for the queue and for the memo. Without a selection the decision buttons are present but inert.
